stem: A 6-year-old boy is brought in for a persistent sore on the side of his neck that has not healed over about three weeks, despite his mother cleaning it daily and applying an antiseptic ointment. It started as a small lump that later broke down into a shallow ulcer with intermittent thin discharge. He has a history of mild eczema, and his mother initially thought this was simply another eczema flare in an unusual location. He has had occasional low-grade fevers. No known TB contact in the household. No prior TB treatment, no known drug-resistant contact. A swab and biopsy of the sinus tract were obtained; tissue was sent for molecular testing, which was positive for M. tuberculosis. Exam: a 1.5 cm shallow ulcer with undermined edges over the left neck, connecting to a firm underlying lymph node, mild surrounding eczema elsewhere on his arms.

patient.social_history: Lives with parents; mother initially self-managed the neck lesion as an eczema flare
patient.presenting_complaint: Non-healing neck ulcer with intermittent discharge, occasional low-grade fevers
patient.exam_findings: 1.5 cm shallow ulcer with undermined edges over left neck connecting to a firm lymph node, mild eczema elsewhere
patient.prior_treatment: Daily wound cleaning and antiseptic ointment at home; no prior TB treatment

distractors: The sinus and ulcer treated as an atypical eczema flare given his known history, delaying recognition of a distinct process
A superficial bacterial skin infection proposed as the cause of the discharge, prompting a course of topical antibiotics rather than tissue sampling
ntep_correct_actions: Perform upfront molecular testing (NAAT) directly on the accessible extrapulmonary specimen (the sinus tract tissue/aspirate) as the first-line microbiological tool, rather than anchoring the workup around culture and histology as the primary reference standard.

us_correct_actions: Anchor the diagnostic workup for this extrapulmonary presentation around culture and histology as the reference standard, treating molecular testing as a general, conditional adjunct rather than the upfront first-line tool for extrapulmonary specimens.
critical_error_conditions: Attributing the non-healing ulcer entirely to his known eczema and deferring tissue sampling and molecular testing
expected_divergence_points: Whether upfront molecular testing on the accessible extrapulmonary specimen is the first-line diagnostic tool or culture/histology remains the anchoring reference standard
